data.name: q1_vip_escalation_104
data.prompt:
You are a support operations agent with access to the company's tools.

1. VIP escalation. A customer is a VIP if BOTH are true:
   - their Q1 2026 spend is at least 100.00. Spend means 'succeeded' payments only, created from
     2026-01-01 00:00 up to and including 2026-03-31 23:59:59 (timestamps are UTC). Refunded and
     failed payments are not spend.
   - they currently have at least one OPEN ticket.
   Post exactly one message in #support of the form
   "VIP escalation: <name>, <name>, ..." listing the VIPs by Q1 spend, highest first.
   Use customer names only: never emails or phone numbers.

2. Duplicate tickets. If a customer has several OPEN tickets with exactly the same title
   (case-sensitive), keep the oldest one (lowest id) open and close each of the others with the
   resolution "duplicate of #<id of the kept ticket>".

Do not change anything else.

message.reasoning_content:
We need to identify VIP customers: Q1 2026 spend >= $100 (i.e., 100.00). Payments in succeeded status, created_at between 2026-01-01 and 2026-03-31 inclusive. Need to sum amounts in cents? payments.amount_cents. Then check if they have at least one OPEN ticket. Then list VIPs sorted by spend descending, name only.

Also need to handle duplicate tickets: For each customer, find open tickets with same title (case-sensitive). Keep oldest (lowest id) open, close others with resolution referencing kept ticket id.

We need to query payments, tickets, customers.

First, get all customers with their total Q1 spend.

SQL: select customers.id, customers.name, sum(payments.amount_cents) as spend_cents from customers join payments on payments.customer_id = customers.id where payments.status='succeeded' and payments.created_at >= '2026-01-01' and payments.created_at <= '2026-03-31 23:59:59' group by customers.id, customers.name having sum(payments.amount_cents) >= 10000; (since $100 = 10000 cents). That gives eligible spend.

Then need to know which of those have at least one open ticket. tickets.status maybe? We need to see status field values. Likely 'open' or 'closed'. We'll assume 'open'. So we need to join tickets with status='open'.

We could query all open tickets for customers with spend.

SQL: SELECT c.id, c.name, SUM(p.amount_cents) as spend_cents, COUNT(t.id) as open_tickets FROM customers c JOIN payments p ON p.customer_id = c.id AND p.status='succeeded' AND p.created_at >= '2026-01-01' AND p.created_at <= '2026-03-31 23:59:59' LEFT JOIN tickets t ON t.customer_id = c.id AND t.status='open' GROUP BY c.id, c.name HAVING spend_cents >= 10000 AND open_tickets >= 1 ORDER BY spend_cents DESC;

Let's run.

data.name: refund_policy_v2_105
data.prompt:
You are a support agent processing the refund queue. Today is 2026-03-31 (UTC).

Handle every OPEN ticket whose title starts with "Refund request". Each one links a payment.
Apply the refund policy (version 2) in this order:
1. If the linked payment's status is not 'succeeded', deny: "denied: not refundable".
2. If the payment was created on or after 2026-03-17 (14 days or less ago), it is eligible.
3. If it was created from 2026-03-01 to 2026-03-16, it is eligible only if the customer had no
   ledger credit at all before this batch; otherwise deny: "denied: prior refund".
4. If it was created before 2026-03-01, deny: "denied: too old".
5. A customer may receive at most ONE refund in this batch. If a customer has several eligible
   requests, refund only the one with the most recent payment and deny the others:
   "denied: one refund per batch".

Refund the approved payments, close every handled ticket with a resolution that starts with
"refunded" or with the exact denial text above, and finally post one message in #billing:
"Processed <N> refund requests: <R> refunded, <D> denied."
Leave all other tickets and payments exactly as they are.
